title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (first page of a dated note '15.1.', probably January 1984, in the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' dossier). X is a smooth curve of type (g,ν) over Q̄: genus g with ν punctures, presumably hyperbolic. Y is a stable but non-smooth curve of the same type (g,ν). It carries a 'propagateur' N; 'normal' is crossed out.

What N is. In modern terms N is most plausibly a choice, at each node, of smoothing data: a nonzero element, or at least an argument/direction, of T_p ⊗ T_q of the two branches. Equivalently it is a log structure of 'standard log point' type on Y, or a point of the real-oriented blow-up of the Deligne–Mumford boundary over [Y]. Such data define a modified fundamental group π1([Y,N]), written as 'groupe fondamental cat.' over a crossed-out 'modifié'. This is the fundamental group of the space obtained by replacing each node by a circle (a cylinder). In modern language it is the Kato–Nakayama / log fundamental group of the log curve. It is isomorphic, as an outer group, to the profinite fundamental group of a nearby smooth fibre.

Teichmüller isomorphism. φ: X ≃_T Y is a 'Teichmüller isomorphism': an isotopy class of identification of the underlying marked surfaces, collapsing the vanishing cycles onto the nodes. In other words a marking of both by the same reference surface, so that [Y,N] is a boundary point of augmented Teichmüller space, decorated by N. First NB: φ induces an isomorphism of exterior (outer) profinite groups π1(X) → π1([Y,N]). Grothendieck adds, with a hesitant reading, that φ is determined by this outer isomorphism.

Base points. If one fixes base points (ordinary points or 'points at infinity', i.e. tangential base points at cusps) on X and on [Y,N], one gets the notion of a Teichmüller isomorphism respecting the marked points. The two base points must be of the same kind: both at finite distance, or both at infinity. Grothendieck warns that base points on [Y,N] are somewhat distinct from the singular points of Y; they can lie on the inserted circles. Such a φ gives a genuine isomorphism of (profinite) groups π1(X,x) → π1([Y,N],y).

Galois warning. Even the outer isomorphism is not compatible with the outer actions of Gal(Q̄/K), K a sufficiently large finite subextension of Q̄/Q. This is to be expected. On π1([Y,N]) Galois acts through the degenerate ('Tate-type' / tangential-at-boundary) action. There the vanishing-cycle subgroups are normalized with cyclotomic action. Nothing of the sort holds for an arbitrary smooth X.

Final NB. Bring out three conjugacy classes (types) of homomorphisms Ẑ(1) → π1(X), only two when ν = 0. The most plausible reading is: cusp inertia (the 'bouts', absent when ν = 0), plus loops of simple closed curves of two kinds (perhaps separating vs non-separating, i.e. potential vanishing cycles).

The next page makes the programme explicit:
- (a) extend the fundamental anabelian conjecture to singular stable (or more general) anabelian curves;
- (b) recover Sing(Y) ∪ {missing points} as the conjugacy classes of subgroups ≅ Ẑ of π1(Y) normalized by π1(K), acting through the cyclotomic character;
- (c) define anabelian compactifications modeled on Deligne–Mumford, and study their behaviour under specialization.

The page thus serves the project of tying the Teichmüller tower / surgery picture (Esquisse) to Galois actions at the boundary of moduli and to anabelian geometry of degenerate curves.
errors: 'K extension finie de Q̄/Q' should be read as K a finite subextension of Q̄/Q, i.e. a number field inside Q̄. This is a slip of notation, not of mathematics.

The claim that the Teichmüller isomorphism is 'determined by' the outer isomorphism is only correct up to the usual caveats. For profinite outer isomorphisms one needs injectivity of the mapping class group into Out of the profinite π1, which is known. But not every profinite outer isomorphism comes from a topological Teichmüller isomorphism.
The remark on base points is necessary: for nodes, a base point on [Y,N] lying on an inserted circle is not a point of Y. The text flags this but does not define it precisely.
The 'three classes' count is unproven on the page and the reading of the last phrase is uncertain.

ideas.what: Modified ('categorical') fundamental group π1([Y,N]) of a stable curve Y equipped with smoothing/propagator data N at the nodes, isomorphic to π1 of a nearby smooth fibre
ideas.modern_name: log fundamental group of a log stable curve / Kato–Nakayama space; fundamental group at a tangential base point on the DM boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kato–Nakayama, Illusie, Fujiwara–Kato (log étale π1); Ihara–Nakamura (1997) for Galois actions on maximally degenerate marked curves; Mochizuki (semi-graphs of anabelioids)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses surgery, the Teichmüller tower and tangential base points at infinity, but not this precise construction as far as I know

ideas.what: Teichmüller isomorphism between a smooth curve and a decorated stable curve, inducing an outer (and, with base points, actual) isomorphism of profinite π1
ideas.modern_name: marking / point of augmented Teichmüller space (real-oriented blow-up of the DM boundary); specialization isomorphism of π1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bers, Abikoff (augmented Teichmüller space); SGA1 for tame specialization; Ihara–Nakamura
ideas.where_published: related ideas in Esquisse d'un programme (§3, Teichmüller tower, surgery)

ideas.what: Observation that the outer isomorphism is not Galois-equivariant for the outer Galois actions
ideas.modern_name: difference between Galois action at a tangential boundary point (degenerate, Tate-type) and on a generic smooth fibre

ideas.what: Distinguished conjugacy classes of homomorphisms Ẑ(1) → π1(X) (cuspidal inertia vs loops of simple closed curves), with a group-theoretic recovery of nodes and cusps as Ẑ-subgroups normalized by Galois with cyclotomic action (next page)
ideas.modern_name: group-theoretic characterization of cuspidal and nodal (edge-like) subgroups; combinatorial anabelian geometry; Galois-theoretic recovery of the dual semi-graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (cuspidal inertia), Mochizuki ('Semi-graphs of anabelioids', 2006), Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, 2009–)

ideas.what: Extension of the anabelian conjecture to singular stable curves and notion of 'anabelian compactification' modeled on Deligne–Mumford (next page)
ideas.modern_name: anabelian geometry of log stable curves / of moduli boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (log-anabelian results for stable curves over finite and p-adic fields)

missed.claim: Already in 1983–84, Grothendieck links the surgery / augmented-Teichmüller picture to anabelian geometry of degenerate curves. Decorated stable curves [Y,N] carry profinite π1, and nodes and cusps should be recoverable as Galois-normalized Ẑ(1)-subgroups. This anticipates Ihara–Nakamura's boundary Galois actions and Mochizuki/Hoshi–Mochizuki combinatorial anabelian geometry by over a decade.
missed.quote: Mettre en évidence trois classes de conjugaison d'homs. Ẑ(1) → π1(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's priority of formulation for the anabelian conjecture for stable/log curves. It also gives an independent motivation from conformal surgery. This is historiographically relevant and not acknowledged in the literature.

missed.claim: A notion of Teichmüller isomorphism with marked base points of 'the same kind' (finite or at infinity), including base points on the inserted circles of [Y,N]. This would give genuine (not just outer) isomorphisms. It amounts to a groupoid of tangential base points on the boundary of moduli, sketched but not worked out here.
missed.quote: on a une notion d'isom de Teichmüller respect. à les pts marqués ... (tous deux à distance finie, ou tous deux à l'infini)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Related to the construction of the profinite Teichmüller groupoid with base points on the DM boundary (Nakamura–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps). The precise inclusion of circle-points as base points may be a slightly different framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is mostly a setup, and the main ideas were later developed independently (Ihara–Nakamura, Mochizuki). Still, it is an unpublished early formulation of anabelian geometry for degenerate stable curves, with Galois-characterized nodal/cuspidal subgroups, tied to the surgery picture, which has historical value.
transcription_corrections: 'Quand on se donne' — confirmed. The phrase 'respect. à les pts marqués' is more likely 'respectant les pts marqués'.
'K ss/ extension finie' is likely 'K sous-extension finie de Q̄/Q'.
The final quoted word '4-bouts' is uncertain; it is probably '"bouts"' (the ends, i.e. cusps), consistent with 'deux seulement si ν = 0'.
'(pro cat.!)' could also read '(pas cat.!)'; uncertain.
Inserted 'cat.' replaces crossed-out 'modifié' in 'groupe fondamental cat. π1([Y,N])'.
